title: Rates: Unit Rates, Speed and Best Buys
seo_title: Year 8 Rates Worksheets: Unit Rates, Speed, Distance and Time and Best Buys (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: recognise and use rates to solve problems involving the comparison of 2 related quantities of different units of measure
meta_desc: Free Year 8 maths worksheets on rates for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M8M05): unit rates, speed, distance and time, converting km/h and m/s, best buys and fuel problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A rate compares two quantities with different units, such as km/h or $/kg.
key_sub: Speed = distance ÷ time. To compare value, find the price for the same amount.
body_html:
How it works

A rate compares two quantities with different units, such as km/h, $/kg or L/min. A unit rate compares to 1 unit: divide the first quantity by the second.

Speed = distance ÷ time, distance = speed × time, time = distance ÷ speed. Change minutes to hours by dividing by 60: 45 minutes = 0.75 hours, not 0.45.

To find the best buy, compare the price for the same amount of each pack.

Example

A car travels 210 km in 3 hours. Find its average speed.

210 ÷ 3 = 70.

Answer: 70 km/h

Example

Convert 72 km/h into m/s.

72 km/h = 72 000 m in 3600 s.

72 000 ÷ 3600.

Answer: 20 m/s

Example

Which is better value: 500 g for $4.50 or 1 kg for $8.40?

$0.90 per 100 g and $0.84 per 100 g.

Answer: The 1 kg pack

Common mistakes

  • Dividing the wrong way: $45 for 3 hours is $15 per hour, not 0.07 hours per dollar.
  • Treating minutes as decimals: 1 hour 30 minutes is 1.5 hours, not 1.3 hours.
  • Choosing the cheapest pack instead of the cheapest price per unit.
  • Multiplying by 3.6 to change km/h to m/s. Divide by 3.6.

faq.q: What is a rate in maths?
faq.a: A rate compares two quantities measured in different units, such as 60 km per hour or $4 per kilogram.
A rate for 1 unit of the second quantity. $45 for 3 hours is a unit rate of $15 per hour.

faq.q: How do I convert km/h to m/s?
faq.a: Multiply by 1000 to get metres and divide by 3600 to get seconds, which is the same as dividing by 3.6.

faq.q: How do I work out the best buy?
faq.a: Find the price per unit (or per 100 g) for each pack. The lower unit price is the better value.
